Two memorable battles for the lead occurred in the July 15 200 mile late model stock car race here at
state fair park. First, Don White, Keokuk, Ia. (#4-1962 Zecol-Lubaid Ford) roared past A. J. Foyt, Houston, Tex.
(#7-Nichels Engineering Pontiac) on the 14th mile. Foyt had led from the first turn but could not stave off
White's challenges. White came on to win the race.
White later was pressed by Paul Goldsmith, St, Clair Shores, Mich. (#1 - 1962 Nichels Engineering Pontiac)
who went into the lead. Goldsmith then found himself challenged by Norm Nelson, Racine, Wis. (#2 - 1962
Wynn Oil Ford) as both are seen lapping Mike Klapak, Warren, Ohio (#52 - 1962 Ford) near the 80 mile mark.
Goldsmith fought off Nelson until both came to the pits for gas on the 100th mile. Nelson then led until the
197 mile when he was forced in again for gas. Goldsmith burned a valve on his car and drove to finish the
race, coming in fifth.

BAY DARNELL
Deerfield, III.
Bay Darnell made his first appearance in a
national championship late model stock car race
here in the July 15 200 miler and finished a credit-
able 14th. Has competed in several races on the
United States Auto Club late model circuit this
summer. Bay is no stranger to Milwaukee fans
having raced here many times in modified stock
cars and has scored one feature race victory.
NEIL HOUSTON
Des Plaines, III.
Likeable Neil Houston had rough going in the
July 15 200 mile stock car race here but still
managed to finish 20th. Was running in the first
10 until he was involved in a two car spin with
Troy Ruttman of Dearborn, Mich. on the 47th
mile. Ruttman's car was out for the day. Houston
had his car inspected and approved and went back
into the race. One of the few drivers in racing to
wear a goatee.

Every precaution is taken to safeguard both pit crewmen and drivers on pit stops for gasoline. Notice
the two fire crewmen keep their equipment in a ready position as the 1962 Ford of Lee Drollinger, Champaign,
Ill. is refuelled. All racing personnel express satisfaction at the safety setup here at state fair park that is
considered by many as the best in the country.

be attributed to quick work in the pits in getting him refuelled and a change of tires in 19 seconds. In fact,
White won the race because a pit stop by Norm Nelson, Racine, Wis. was so fast that he didn't take on enough
fuel and was forced to come in again at 197 miles.

Hot Pursuit
Paul Goldsmith, St. Clair Shores, Mich. (#1 - 1962 Nichels Engineering Pontiac) was just a step ahead of Norm Nelson,
Racine, Wis. (#2 - 1962 Wynn Oil Ford) and Don White, Keokuk, Ia. (#4 - 1962 Zecol-Lubaid Ford) as the three cars roared
toward the 50 mile mark. Goldsmith and Nelson then battled until the 100th mile for the lead. White developed brake trouble
and dropped back but as it turned out had the last word and won the 200 mile race here on July 15.
Lapping slower cars posed a problem for Paul Goldsmith, St. Clair Shores, Mich. (#1 - 1962 Nichels Engineering Pontiac)
and Norm Nelson, Racine, Wis. (#2 - 1962 Wynn Oil Ford) as they battled for the lead in the July 15 200 miler. Goldsmith has
just edged past Bill Cheesbourg, Tucson, Ariz. (#17 - 1962 Ford) as Nelson trails along behind the Arizona driver. Goldsmith
then set sail for Ray Berry, LaGrange, Ill. (#57 - 1960 Chevrolet). All but Berry finished the race.

NO LAUGHING MATTER
It was no laughing matter, at least to Carl
Marchese (right) Chief Steward for Wiscon-
sin Auto Racing, Inc. as he talked to Ray
Nichels, Highland, Ind., manager of the trio
of 1962 Pontiacs driven by Paul Goldsmith,
A. J. Foyt, and Roger Ward in the 200 mile
stock car race that day. Nichels had reason
to smile. Foyt had nailed down third place,
Goldsmith, fifth place, in the July 15 Classic
that paid more than $25,000 in prize and ac-
cessory money.
BOB MEANS PHOTO
44 YEARS OF RACING KNOW-HOW
Nearly a half-century of
racing know-how was concen-
trated in the conversation be-
tween Henry Banks, Director
of Competition for the United
States Auto Club and Norm
Nelson, Racine, second rank-
ing USAC late model stock
car driver just before the July
15 200 mile stock car race here.
Banks raced 21 years in big
cars and midgets. Was national
AAA big car champion in
1950. Nelson, in his 23rd year
since he drove his first race is
the acknowledged king of the
stocks at Milwaukee with
seven victories and more than
$45,000 in gross earnings to
his credit. He was National
USAC Stock Car Champ in
1960.
